title: Find the Count of Numbers Which Are Not Special
summary: Given two positive integers l and r, count the numbers in the range [l, r] that do not have exactly two proper divisors.
statement: Given two positive integers l and r, count the numbers in the range [l, r] that do not have exactly two proper divisors. A number is special if it has precisely two proper divisors, like 4 (divisors: 1, 2), but not 6 (divisors: 1, 2, 3).
constraints: A special number has exactly two positive proper divisors, excluding itself.
Return how many integers in the inclusive range are not special.
hints: A number has exactly two proper divisors iff it is p² for a prime p: its divisors are 1,p,p².
Sieve primes through floor(sqrt(r)) and count whose squares fall in [l,r].
Return range size minus qualifying prime-square count.
Composite bases add more divisors, and nonsquares cannot have exactly the paired divisor structure, so prime squares characterize all special numbers.
editorial: Composite bases add more divisors, and nonsquares cannot have exactly the paired divisor structure, so prime squares characterize all special numbers.

tests.explanation: None of five, six, or seven has exactly two proper divisors, so all three are non-special.
Only 4 and 9 are squares of primes and therefore special; eight numbers are not.
